document.title: Strategic Thoughts
document.authors: Office of the Secretary of Defense (Rumsfeld)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), New Documents Detail America's Strategic Response to 9/11
document.note: [Top Secret/Close Hold] Rumsfeld advises President Bush to think beyond al-Qaeda in Afghanistan, favoring equip-and-train efforts with local opposition forces and humanitarian aid over aerial strikes. He argues the war must 'significantly change the world's political map', with new regimes in Afghanistan and another state that supports terrorism.

Rumsfeld sends the 'Strategic Thoughts' memorandum to the President. It proposes indirect action through local opposition forces and care over initial air strikes. It also proposes aiming to change regimes that support terrorism.
Rumsfeld sends memorandum 'Strategic Thoughts' to the President proposing indirect action via local opposition forces, equip-and-train activities and limited initial air strikes.
Air strikes against Al-Qaida and Taliban targets are planned to begin soon, per memo.
September 11 attacks on the US, referenced as the basis for the war aim.

key_claims: The memo proposes that US action in the initial period be indirect, working through local non-US forces and opposition groups, rather than direct aerial attack.
Initial air strikes should be restrained until intelligence allows worthwhile strikes on al-Qaida and other targets, ideally coordinated to support the opposition.
The US should avoid images of Americans killing Muslims and instead present the targets as enemies of Muslims themselves.
A key war aim is to persuade or compel states to stop supporting terrorism, and to threaten their regimes by partnering with their opponents.
The memo envisions new regimes in Afghanistan and one or two other states that support terrorism, plus Syria out of Lebanon and the end of WMD programmes.
The memo notes that public expectations assume an immediate US strike exclusively on al-Qaida in Afghanistan, and argues it would be more impressive to build forces patiently and act elsewhere first.
